# MACE: Multicore Agentic Co-Design Engine

> MACE is an LLM-agent system that turns a single-core design into a verified multicore OpenPiton system: it plans, builds and simulates OpenPiton meshes on the CHIA framework from a hardware objective written in English.

MACE has two parts. `chia_openpiton` is a CHIA adapter for OpenPiton's configure, build, run, and collect operations, and imports nothing from `mace`. `mace` is the agentic loop on top of it: a planner, parallel task execution, a Verilator verification gate, failure analysis, and replanning. The loop passes 2x2 and 4x4 meshes of Ariane (CVA6) and PicoRV32 in Verilator simulation.

## Documentation

- [MACE User Manual](https://ranaumarnadeem.github.io/MACE/01_mace_user/index.html): installing MACE, running the loop and the baselines, and reading the results
- [MACE Requirements Specification](https://ranaumarnadeem.github.io/MACE/02_mace_requirements/mace_requirements_specification.html): what MACE must do
- [MACE Design Document](https://ranaumarnadeem.github.io/MACE/03_mace_design/index.html): planning, parallel task execution, integration, verification, and failure analysis in the MACE loop
- [chia_openpiton Adapter](https://ranaumarnadeem.github.io/MACE/04_chia_openpiton/index.html): how the loop builds and runs OpenPiton
- [Supported Cores](https://ranaumarnadeem.github.io/MACE/05_mace_cores/index.html): the three OpenPiton cores (Ariane, OpenSPARC T1, and PicoRV32) and how to add another
- [MACE Evaluation](https://ranaumarnadeem.github.io/MACE/06_mace_evaluation/index.html): the baselines, results, and cost measurements

## Related projects

- [OpenPiton](https://github.com/PrincetonUniversity/openpiton): the manycore research framework MACE builds on
- [CHIA](https://github.com/ucb-bar/chia): the agentic hardware framework MACE extends
